### Atlas.metadata

```python
Atlas.metadata() -> dict[str, Any]
```

How the scanned store was made: its ``provenance.json`` (docs/format.md section
9), as a ``dict``.

Keys: ``kyto_version``, ``dependencies``, ``plan`` (the plan JSON whose output
the store holds, without its sink, or ``None`` for an import; ``provenance()``
rebuilds it), ``source``, ``seeds``, ``device`` and ``run`` (start, end and
seconds per step).
It describes the store this plan scans, not the plan's own steps
(``to_json()``). kyto stores no free-form metadata such as anndata's ``uns``.

Returns
-------
dict
    A new dict the caller owns, read from the store (no matrix data).

Raises
------
StoreIOError
    ``KY-E110``: the store has no readable ``provenance.json``.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).metadata()["source"]["kind"]
'mtx'

### Atlas.provenance

```python
Atlas.provenance() -> Atlas
```

The plan that wrote the scanned store, rebuilt from its ``provenance.json``
(docs/format.md section 9).

A store written by ``sink_zarr`` records the plan whose output it holds, with
every name resolved (R6) and every seed (R7). This is that plan, without the
sink: its scan reads the store the original plan read, at the path recorded
then. Sinking it again with the same kyto version writes a store with the same
bytes, apart from the ``run`` object of ``provenance.json`` (start, end and
per-step timings) (R11).

Returns
-------
Atlas
    A new plan; nothing is read but ``provenance.json`` (no matrix data).

Raises
------
LineageError
    ``KY-E304``: the store holds no plan (an import from ``convert``), or its
    ``provenance.json`` cannot be read.

Examples
--------
>>> target = store.parent / "logged.kyto"
>>> scan(store).log1p(layer="counts", into="log1p").sink_zarr(target)
>>> print(scan(target).provenance())
LOG1P "counts" -> "log1p"
SCAN "..." (2 cells x 3 genes)
>>> scan(target).provenance().sink_zarr(store.parent / "again.kyto")
>>> scan(store).provenance()
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
kyto.errors.LineageError: KY-E304: provenance() cannot rebuild the plan that wrote store '...'...

### Atlas.to_json

```python
Atlas.to_json() -> str
```

Write the plan as JSON text, to store it or send it elsewhere.

The text is versioned (``"version": 1``) and lists the plan's nodes from the
scan up, each with its stable ID (its position from the scan, 0), the ID of its
input, and its step: the plan method that built it and its arguments with every
name resolved in full (R6). The scan holds the store's location, its schema and
its gene IDs and symbols as read when the plan was built, so ``from_json`` needs
no store. Equal plans write equal text, and ``from_json(atlas.to_json())``
gives back an equal plan.

Returns
-------
str
    The plan JSON, on one line (a new string; the plan is unchanged). Nothing
    is read.

Examples
--------
>>> genes = gene_column("feature_type") == "Gene Expression"
>>> atlas = scan(store).filter(genes)
>>> text = atlas.to_json()
>>> text[:39]
'{"format":"kyto-plan","version":1,"node'
>>> print(from_json(text))
FILTER_GENES gene_column('feature_type') == 'Gene Expression'
SCAN "..." (2 cells x 3 genes)

### Atlas.explain

```python
Atlas.explain(*, format: Literal['text'] = 'text', threads: int | None = None) -> str
Atlas.explain(*, format: Literal['json'], threads: int | None = None) -> Explanation
```

How the plan would run: its logical and optimized trees (task 4.7).

The logical tree lists the plan's steps from the last down to the scan, each with
its node ID and its parameters, every name resolved in full as the plan stored it
(R6: a ``feature`` or a gene read by symbol shows the gene ID and layer it
names), and, in brackets, a note when the step has a cheaper alternative (a
centred ``scale`` stores every gene of every cell; PCA centres sparse data
implicitly). The optimized tree is the plan optimized with every rule (for a terminal
reading all of its output): one line for what the output reads, then one line per
node from the top down to the scan, each with the logical nodes it came from
(``(node 1, 2)`` for a fused pass) and, in brackets, how it runs: ``device``
(``cpu``), ``passes`` over its input's blocks (with the ``statistics`` passes over
all cells and the ``apply`` pass when there are statistics passes), and
``blocks=N cells`` (streamed in blocks of N cells: the store's cell block size,
or smaller on more than 2 ``threads``), ``in memory`` or ``no data``, then
``input held`` for a step that holds its input in
memory (task 5.12: it reads the store once, and its ``passes`` run over the held
blocks). ``estimate()`` gives the cost of the whole plan. Nothing is read.

Parameters
----------
format : {"text", "json"}, default="text"
    ``"text"``: the two trees as text, under ``logical plan`` and ``optimized
    plan``. ``"json"``: the same as a dict with ``logical`` (one dict per step:
    ``id``, ``name``, ``parameters``, ``input``, ``note``) and ``optimized`` (``outputs``:
    ``node``, ``reads``; ``nodes``: ``index``, ``name``, ``parameters``,
    ``reads`` (a scan's, else ``None``), ``input``, ``origin``, ``device``,
    ``passes``, ``statistics_passes``, ``apply_pass``, ``blocks`` (``"cells"``,
    ``"in_memory"`` or ``"none"``), ``block_cells`` and ``holds_input``), in the
    text's order.
threads : int or None, default=None
    Show the plan a run on this many threads without ``memory_limit`` uses (task
    5.14: on more than 2 threads one block in flight per thread, each smaller, so
    the cells in flight stay those of 2 store cell blocks); ``None`` shows 2 blocks
    in flight of the store's cell blocks, the same on every machine.

Returns
-------
str or dict
    A ``str`` for ``format="text"``, a ``dict`` for ``format="json"``; new
    objects each call (the plan is unchanged).

Raises
------
PlanError
    ``KY-E215``: ``format`` is not ``"text"`` or ``"json"``.

Examples
--------
>>> genes = gene_column("feature_type") == "Gene Expression"
>>> print(scan(store).filter(genes).explain())
logical plan
  node 1 FILTER_GENES gene_column('feature_type') == 'Gene Expression' <- node 0
  node 0 SCAN "..." (2 cells x 3 genes)
optimized plan
  output #1 reads [...]
  #1 FILTER_GENES ... <- #0 (node 1) [device=cpu passes=1 blocks=4096 cells]
  #0 SCAN ... (node 0) [device=cpu passes=1 blocks=4096 cells]
>>> explained = scan(store).filter(genes).explain(format="json")
>>> [step["name"] for step in explained["logical"]]
['FILTER_GENES', 'SCAN']
>>> explained["optimized"]["nodes"][0]["passes"]
1
>>> scan(store).explain(format="json", threads=10)["optimized"]["nodes"][0]["block_cells"]
820

### Atlas.estimate

```python
Atlas.estimate(*, threads: int | None = None) -> CostEstimate
```

What running the plan would cost, from its schema alone (task 4.6).

Estimated for the plan as ``explain(threads=threads)`` shows it (every
optimizer rule, a terminal reading all of its output, the CPU; one cell block in
flight per thread, smaller blocks on more than 2 threads, so the cells in flight
stay those of 2 store cell blocks, task 5.14; on more than 2 threads the
estimated peak is high, up to about 1.5x the 2-thread one, never low).
``passes`` counts the passes over the store's matrix: each statistics pass
streams the data again from the store (once for all of a step's statistics passes
when it holds its input, below), and one more pass delivers what is read from the
stream. ``bytes_read`` is the decoded size of the matrix tiles those
passes read (fewer bytes are on disk, compressed; the cell and gene tables are
not counted). ``peak_memory`` is the most memory the plan holds at once: the
blocks in flight in every streamed step (sized for blocks of mean density) plus
statistics and in-memory results; the store reader's part is within 25% of
what it allocates on the test fixtures. A step with several statistics passes
(``pca``, ``highly_variable_genes`` with ``seurat_v3``) holds its input in
memory and reads it from the store once (task 5.12; ``explain()`` says ``input
held``): ``held_memory`` is what those inputs hold (part of ``peak_memory``) and
``passes_saved`` the passes over the store they save. Under a ``memory_limit``
the input is held only if the plan still fits. Nothing is read.

Parameters
----------
threads : int or None, default=None
    Estimate a run on this many threads without ``memory_limit`` (as
    ``explain(threads=...)``); ``None`` for 2 blocks in flight of the store's
    cell blocks, the same on every machine.

Returns
-------
CostEstimate
    A new dict with ``passes``, ``bytes_read``, ``peak_memory`` and
    ``held_memory`` (bytes, as ``int``), ``passes_saved`` and ``device``
    (``"cpu"``).

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).estimate()  # doctest: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE
{'passes': 1, 'bytes_read': 16428, 'peak_memory': 1048592, 'held_memory': 0,
 'passes_saved': 0, 'device': 'cpu'}

### Embedding

```python
class Embedding
```

An embedding of a plan, a dense array with one row per cell or gene: read-only and
lazy.

Taken from ``Atlas.embedding(name)``. It reads nothing: ``names()``, ``schema()``
and ``estimate()`` answer from metadata, and the terminals ``to_numpy()`` and
``to_torch(device=...)`` run the plan (task 7.3). An embedding is stored dense, so ``to_numpy()`` densifies nothing (R8). It has no method that changes it or the plan (R2).

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store_with_members).embedding("X_pca")
<Embedding 'X_pca': 2 cells x 2 components, float32>

### Embedding.names

```python
Embedding.names() -> list[str]
```

The column names: ``<embedding>:<component>`` for each component, from 0.

Returns
-------
list of str
    A new list; reads no data. For a cell embedding these are the full names
    ``feature(...)`` accepts (docs/feature_names.md).

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store_with_members).embedding("X_pca").names()
['X_pca:0', 'X_pca:1']

### Embedding.schema

```python
Embedding.schema() -> EmbeddingSchema
```

The embedding's entry in ``schema.json`` (format.md section 8).

Returns
-------
dict
    A new dict with ``name``, ``axis`` (``"cells"`` or ``"genes"``), ``width``
    and ``dtype`` (``"float32"`` or ``"float64"``). Changing it changes nothing
    else.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store_with_members).embedding("X_pca").schema()
{'name': 'X_pca', 'axis': 'cells', 'width': 2, 'dtype': 'float32'}

### Embedding.estimate

```python
Embedding.estimate() -> Estimate
```

What the embedding looks like, from metadata alone (no data is read).

Returns
-------
dict
    A new dict: ``n_rows`` (cells or genes), ``n_columns`` (components), ``nnz``
    (``None``: it is dense) and ``dense_bytes`` (what ``to_numpy`` would
    allocate). A value not known without running the plan is ``None``.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store_with_members).embedding("X_pca").estimate()
{'n_rows': 2, 'n_columns': 2, 'nnz': None, 'dense_bytes': 16}

### Embedding.to_numpy

```python
Embedding.to_numpy(*, memory_limit: str | int | None = None, threads: int | None = None, progress: Callable[[int, int], object] | None = None) -> numpy.NDArray[numpy.float32 | numpy.float64]
```

Run the plan and return the embedding as a NumPy array.

The embedding after every step of the plan: one row per cell (or gene) the
plan keeps, in store order. It is stored dense, so this densifies nothing (R8).

Parameters
----------
memory_limit : str or int or None, default=None
    The most memory running the plan may use, as ``Atlas.collect`` takes it;
    the result is held in memory besides.
threads : int or None, default=None
    Threads that run the plan; ``None`` for one per CPU core. The result does
    not depend on it (R11).
progress : callable or None, default=None
    Called as ``progress(done, total)`` on the calling thread while the plan
    runs; never for a plain ``scan``, which runs nothing.

Returns
-------
numpy.ndarray
    Rows x components, C order, in the stored dtype; a copy the caller owns
    (R2): read from the store into new memory, handed to NumPy without a
    further copy.

Raises
------
PlanError
    ``KY-E215``: a ``memory_limit``, ``threads`` or ``progress`` that is not
    accepted.
MemoryLimitError
    ``KY-E401``: the plan cannot run within ``memory_limit``.
NotImplementedYetError
    ``KY-E601``: the plan has a step the executor does not run yet.

Examples
--------
>>> atlas = scan(store).log1p(layer="counts", into="log1p").pca(layer="log1p", into="X_pca", n_components=1, seed=0)
>>> array = atlas.embedding("X_pca").to_numpy()
>>> array.shape, array.dtype
((2, 1), dtype('float32'))

### Embedding.to_torch

```python
Embedding.to_torch(*, device: str, memory_limit: str | int | None = None, threads: int | None = None, progress: Callable[[int, int], object] | None = None) -> Any
```

Run the plan and return the embedding as a PyTorch tensor on ``device``.

As ``to_numpy``, then ``torch.from_numpy(array).to(device)``: on the CPU the
tensor shares the new array's memory (no further copy); any other device gets
one more copy, from the host. A tensor made on the device without the host
copy (DLPack) is task 9.5. Needs ``torch`` installed.

Parameters
----------
device : str
    A device PyTorch accepts, such as ``"cpu"``, ``"cuda"``, ``"cuda:1"`` or
    ``"mps"``. Required (R7: the device is always an argument).
memory_limit : str or int or None, default=None
    The most memory running the plan may use, as ``Atlas.collect`` takes it;
    the result is held in memory besides.
threads : int or None, default=None
    Threads that run the plan; ``None`` for one per CPU core. The result does
    not depend on it (R11).
progress : callable or None, default=None
    Called as ``progress(done, total)`` on the calling thread while the plan
    runs; never for a plain ``scan``, which runs nothing.

Returns
-------
torch.Tensor
    Rows x components in the stored dtype, on ``device``; a copy the caller
    owns (R2).

Raises
------
PlanError
    ``KY-E215``: a ``memory_limit``, ``threads`` or ``progress`` that is not
    accepted.
MemoryLimitError
    ``KY-E401``: the plan cannot run within ``memory_limit``.
NotImplementedYetError
    ``KY-E601``: the plan has a step the executor does not run yet.
ModuleNotFoundError
    ``torch`` is not installed.

Examples
--------
>>> atlas = scan(store).log1p(layer="counts", into="log1p").pca(layer="log1p", into="X_pca", n_components=1, seed=0)
>>> atlas.embedding("X_pca").to_torch(device="cpu").shape  # doctest: +SKIP
torch.Size([2, 1])

### Graph

```python
class Graph
```

A graph of a plan, a sparse cells x cells matrix of edge weights: read-only and
lazy.

Taken from ``Atlas.graph(name)``. It reads nothing: ``names()``, ``schema()`` and
``estimate()`` answer from metadata, and the terminals ``to_scipy()`` and
``to_edges()`` run the plan (task 7.3). It has no
method that changes it or the plan (R2).

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store_with_members).graph("connectivities")
<Graph 'connectivities': 2 x 2 cells, nnz 3, float32>

### Graph.names

```python
Graph.names() -> list[str]
```

The column names of its edge list (``to_edges()``).

Returns
-------
list of str
    A new list: ``['source', 'target', 'weight']``.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store_with_members).graph("connectivities").names()
['source', 'target', 'weight']

### Graph.schema

```python
Graph.schema() -> GraphSchema
```

The graph's entry in ``schema.json`` (format.md section 8).

Returns
-------
dict
    A new dict with ``name``, ``axis`` (``"cells"``), ``dtype`` (``"float32"``
    or ``"float64"``) and ``nnz``. Changing it changes nothing else.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store_with_members).graph("connectivities").schema()
{'name': 'connectivities', 'axis': 'cells', 'dtype': 'float32', 'nnz': 3}

### Graph.estimate

```python
Graph.estimate() -> Estimate
```

What the graph looks like, from metadata alone (no data is read).

Returns
-------
dict
    A new dict: ``n_rows`` and ``n_columns`` (cells), ``nnz`` (stored edges)
    and ``dense_bytes`` (a dense cells x cells array). A value not known
    without running the plan is ``None``.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store_with_members).graph("connectivities").estimate()
{'n_rows': 2, 'n_columns': 2, 'nnz': 3, 'dense_bytes': 16}

### Graph.to_scipy

```python
Graph.to_scipy(*, memory_limit: str | int | None = None, threads: int | None = None, progress: Callable[[int, int], object] | None = None) -> scipy.sparse.csr_matrix
```

Run the plan and return the graph as a SciPy CSR matrix.

Parameters
----------
memory_limit : str or int or None, default=None
    The most memory running the plan may use, as ``Atlas.collect`` takes it;
    the result is held in memory besides.
threads : int or None, default=None
    Threads that run the plan; ``None`` for one per CPU core. The result does
    not depend on it (R11).
progress : callable or None, default=None
    Called as ``progress(done, total)`` on the calling thread while the plan
    runs; never for a plain ``scan``, which runs nothing.

Returns
-------
scipy.sparse.csr_matrix
    Cells x cells edge weights in the stored dtype; a copy the caller owns
    (R2), handed over as ``Matrix.to_scipy``'s. A stored edge may weigh 0
    (format.md section 7).

Raises
------
PlanError
    ``KY-E215``: a ``memory_limit``, ``threads`` or ``progress`` that is not
    accepted.
MemoryLimitError
    ``KY-E401``: the plan cannot run within ``memory_limit``.
NotImplementedYetError
    ``KY-E601``: the plan has a step the executor does not run yet.

Examples
--------
>>> atlas = scan(store).log1p(layer="counts", into="log1p").pca(layer="log1p", into="X_pca", n_components=1, seed=0).neighbors("X_pca", n_neighbors=2)
>>> graph = atlas.graph("distances").to_scipy()
>>> graph.shape, graph.dtype
((2, 2), dtype('float32'))

### Graph.to_edges

```python
Graph.to_edges(*, memory_limit: str | int | None = None, threads: int | None = None, progress: Callable[[int, int], object] | None = None) -> polars.DataFrame
```

Run the plan and return the edges as a Polars ``DataFrame``.

Parameters
----------
memory_limit : str or int or None, default=None
    The most memory running the plan may use, as ``Atlas.collect`` takes it;
    the result is held in memory besides.
threads : int or None, default=None
    Threads that run the plan; ``None`` for one per CPU core. The result does
    not depend on it (R11).
progress : callable or None, default=None
    Called as ``progress(done, total)`` on the calling thread while the plan
    runs; never for a plain ``scan``, which runs nothing.

Returns
-------
polars.DataFrame
    One row per stored edge, row by row: ``source`` and ``target`` are cell
    positions (``UInt32``, rows of ``cells.to_polars()`` and of ``to_scipy()``)
    and ``weight`` the stored weight (``Float32`` or ``Float64``); a copy the
    caller owns (R2), handed over as ``Table.to_polars``'s.

Raises
------
PlanError
    ``KY-E215``: a ``memory_limit``, ``threads`` or ``progress`` that is not
    accepted.
MemoryLimitError
    ``KY-E401``: the plan cannot run within ``memory_limit``.
NotImplementedYetError
    ``KY-E601``: the plan has a step the executor does not run yet.

Examples
--------
>>> atlas = scan(store).log1p(layer="counts", into="log1p").pca(layer="log1p", into="X_pca", n_components=1, seed=0).neighbors("X_pca", n_neighbors=2)
>>> atlas.graph("distances").to_edges().columns
['source', 'target', 'weight']

### Matrix

```python
class Matrix
```

A layer of a plan, a sparse cells x genes matrix: read-only and lazy.

Taken from ``Atlas.layer(name)``. It reads nothing: ``names()``, ``schema()`` and
``estimate()`` answer from metadata, and the terminals ``to_scipy()`` and
``to_dense(max_bytes=...)`` run the plan (task 7.3). There is no implicit dense
array (R8): no ``__array__``, and dense output only through ``to_dense``. It has
no method that changes it or the plan (R2).

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).layer("counts")
<Matrix 'counts': 2 cells x 3 genes, nnz 3, uint32>

### Matrix.names

```python
Matrix.names() -> list[str]
```

The column names: the gene IDs, in stored order.

Returns
-------
list of str
    A new list, read from the gene table when the plan was built. After
    a gene ``filter``, the genes that may remain: which ones is known only
    when the plan runs, and ``estimate()`` gives ``n_columns`` as ``None``.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).layer("counts").names()
['ENSG01', 'ENSG02', 'ENSG03']

### Matrix.schema

```python
Matrix.schema() -> LayerSchema
```

The layer's entry in ``schema.json`` (format.md section 8).

Returns
-------
dict
    A new dict with ``name``, ``dtype`` (``"float32"`` or ``"uint32"``) and
    ``nnz``. Changing it changes nothing else.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).layer("counts").schema()
{'name': 'counts', 'dtype': 'uint32', 'nnz': 3}

### Matrix.estimate

```python
Matrix.estimate() -> Estimate
```

What the matrix looks like, from metadata alone (no data is read).

Returns
-------
dict
    A new dict: ``n_rows`` (cells), ``n_columns`` (genes), ``nnz`` (stored
    entries) and ``dense_bytes`` (what ``to_dense`` would allocate). A value not
    known without running the plan is ``None``. The cost estimate (bytes read,
    peak memory) is task 4.6.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).layer("counts").estimate()
{'n_rows': 2, 'n_columns': 3, 'nnz': 3, 'dense_bytes': 24}

### Matrix.to_scipy

```python
Matrix.to_scipy(*, memory_limit: str | int | None = None, threads: int | None = None, progress: Callable[[int, int], object] | None = None) -> scipy.sparse.csr_matrix
```

Run the plan and return the matrix as a SciPy CSR matrix.

The layer after every step of the plan: the cells and genes the plan keeps, in
store order. A plan with steps is run first into a temporary store that holds
only this layer; a plain ``scan`` is read in place. The GIL is released
while the plan runs; Ctrl-C cancels it cleanly.

Parameters
----------
memory_limit : str or int or None, default=None
    The most memory running the plan may use, as ``Atlas.collect`` takes it;
    the result is held in memory besides.
threads : int or None, default=None
    Threads that run the plan; ``None`` for one per CPU core. The result does
    not depend on it (R11).
progress : callable or None, default=None
    Called as ``progress(done, total)`` on the calling thread while the plan
    runs; never for a plain ``scan``, which runs nothing.

Returns
-------
scipy.sparse.csr_matrix
    Cells x genes in the layer's stored dtype (``float32`` or ``uint32``), with
    sorted indices and no stored zeros, ``int32`` index arrays (``int64`` when
    ``nnz`` or the genes need them); a copy the caller owns (R2): the arrays
    hold memory read from the store, handed to NumPy without a further copy
    (one index array is converted to SciPy's dtype).

Raises
------
PlanError
    ``KY-E215``: a ``memory_limit``, ``threads`` or ``progress`` that is not
    accepted.
MemoryLimitError
    ``KY-E401``: the plan cannot run within ``memory_limit``.
NotImplementedYetError
    ``KY-E601``: the plan has a step the executor does not run yet.

Examples
--------
>>> matrix = scan(store).layer("counts").to_scipy()
>>> matrix.shape, matrix.dtype, matrix.nnz
((2, 3), dtype('uint32'), 3)

### Matrix.to_dense

```python
Matrix.to_dense(*, max_bytes: int, memory_limit: str | int | None = None, threads: int | None = None, progress: Callable[[int, int], object] | None = None) -> numpy.NDArray[numpy.float32 | numpy.uint32]
```

Run the plan and return the matrix as a dense NumPy array, if it fits.

The only way to get a dense matrix (R8): absent entries become 0 (R9). When the
size is known from metadata (``estimate()["dense_bytes"]``) it is checked
before the plan runs; otherwise (after a filter) once the plan has run, before
the layer is read.

Parameters
----------
max_bytes : int
    The largest array, in bytes, the caller accepts. Required: there is no
    default, so densifying is always a stated choice. ``estimate()["dense_bytes"]``
    gives the size without reading the matrix.
memory_limit : str or int or None, default=None
    The most memory running the plan may use, as ``Atlas.collect`` takes it;
    the result is held in memory besides.
threads : int or None, default=None
    Threads that run the plan; ``None`` for one per CPU core. The result does
    not depend on it (R11).
progress : callable or None, default=None
    Called as ``progress(done, total)`` on the calling thread while the plan
    runs; never for a plain ``scan``, which runs nothing.

Returns
-------
numpy.ndarray
    Cells x genes, C order, in the layer's stored dtype (``float32`` or
    ``uint32``); a copy the caller owns (R2): densified once into new memory,
    handed to NumPy without a further copy.

Raises
------
MemoryLimitError
    ``KY-E402``: the array is larger than ``max_bytes``, or cannot be
    allocated. ``KY-E401``: the plan cannot run within ``memory_limit``.
PlanError
    ``KY-E215``: a ``max_bytes`` that is not an int of 0 or more, or a
    ``memory_limit``, ``threads`` or ``progress`` that is not accepted.
NotImplementedYetError
    ``KY-E601``: the plan has a step the executor does not run yet.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).layer("counts").to_dense(max_bytes=1024)
array([[5, 0, 1],
       [0, 7, 0]], dtype=uint32)
>>> scan(store).layer("counts").to_dense(max_bytes=8)
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
kyto.errors.MemoryLimitError: KY-E402: 'Matrix.to_dense' cannot allocate a dense 2 x 3 array of 24 bytes: max_bytes is 8...

### Modality

```python
class Modality
```

A modality of a plan, a second feature space on the same cells: read-only and lazy.

Taken from ``Atlas.modality(name)``. Provisional and minimal: store format v0 holds
no modalities, so no store has one yet, and the format version that adds them fixes
the schema and the terminals. It has no method that changes it or the plan (R2).

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).modality("adt")
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
kyto.errors.MissingMemberError: KY-E109: no modality named 'adt' in the store at '...'...

Returns

dict
    A new dict with ``name``, ``n_features``, ``features`` (a table entry) and

What the modality looks like, from metadata alone (no data is read).

    ``dense_bytes`` (``None``).

### Table

```python
class Table
```

The cell or gene table of a plan: read-only and lazy.

Taken from ``Atlas.cells`` or ``Atlas.genes``. It reads nothing: ``names()``,
``schema()`` and ``estimate()`` answer from the schema read when the plan was built,
and the terminals ``to_polars()`` and ``lazy()`` run the plan (task 7.3). It has no
method that changes it or the plan (R2).

Examples
--------
>>> atlas = scan(store)
>>> atlas.cells
<Table cells: 2 rows x 1 columns>

### Table.names

```python
Table.names() -> list[str]
```

The column names, ID column first, in stored order.

Returns
-------
list of str
    A new list; reads no data.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).genes.names()
['gene_id', 'symbol', 'feature_type']

### Table.schema

```python
Table.schema() -> TableSchema
```

The table's entry in ``schema.json`` (format.md section 8).

Returns
-------
dict
    A new ``{"columns": [...]}`` dict, one dict per column with ``name`` and
    ``dtype``, ``n_categories`` and ``ordered`` for an ``Enum`` column, and
    ``lineage`` when the store records one. Changing it changes nothing else.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).cells.schema()
{'columns': [{'name': 'cell_id', 'dtype': 'String'}]}

### Table.estimate

```python
Table.estimate() -> Estimate
```

What the table looks like, from metadata alone (no data is read).

Returns
-------
dict
    A new dict: ``n_rows`` (cells or genes), ``n_columns``, ``nnz`` (``None``)
    and ``dense_bytes`` (``None``: string sizes are not in the schema). A value
    not known without running the plan is ``None``. The cost estimate (bytes
    read, peak memory) is task 4.6.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).genes.estimate()
{'n_rows': 3, 'n_columns': 3, 'nnz': None, 'dense_bytes': None}

### Table.to_polars

```python
Table.to_polars(*, memory_limit: str | int | None = None, threads: int | None = None, progress: Callable[[int, int], object] | None = None) -> polars.DataFrame
```

Run the plan and return the table as a Polars ``DataFrame``.

The table after every step of the plan: its rows are the cells (or genes) the
plan keeps, in store order, and its columns those of ``names()``, computed
columns included. A plan with steps is run first into a temporary store that
holds only this table; a plain ``scan`` is read in place. The GIL is released
while the plan runs; Ctrl-C cancels it cleanly.

Parameters
----------
memory_limit : str or int or None, default=None
    The most memory running the plan may use, as ``Atlas.collect`` takes it;
    the result is held in memory besides.
threads : int or None, default=None
    Threads that run the plan; ``None`` for one per CPU core. The result does
    not depend on it (R11).
progress : callable or None, default=None
    Called as ``progress(done, total)`` on the calling thread while the plan
    runs; never for a plain ``scan``, which runs nothing.

Returns
-------
polars.DataFrame
    A copy the caller owns (R2): read from the store into new memory that is
    handed to Polars without a further copy (the Arrow C stream interface), so
    changing it never changes the store or a later read. String columns are
    ``Enum``, as stored.

Raises
------
PlanError
    ``KY-E215``: a ``memory_limit``, ``threads`` or ``progress`` that is not
    accepted.
MemoryLimitError
    ``KY-E401``: the plan cannot run within ``memory_limit``.
NotImplementedYetError
    ``KY-E601``: the plan has a step the executor does not run yet.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).genes.to_polars()["gene_id"].to_list()
['ENSG01', 'ENSG02', 'ENSG03']

### Table.lazy

```python
Table.lazy(*, memory_limit: str | int | None = None, threads: int | None = None, progress: Callable[[int, int], object] | None = None) -> polars.LazyFrame
```

Run the plan and return the table as a Polars ``LazyFrame``.

Runs the plan now, as ``to_polars`` (the table's schema, such as the
categories of an ``Enum`` column, is known only then), and returns a lazy
query over the result, to go on with in Polars.

Parameters
----------
memory_limit : str or int or None, default=None
    The most memory running the plan may use, as ``Atlas.collect`` takes it;
    the result is held in memory besides.
threads : int or None, default=None
    Threads that run the plan; ``None`` for one per CPU core. The result does
    not depend on it (R11).
progress : callable or None, default=None
    Called as ``progress(done, total)`` on the calling thread while the plan
    runs; never for a plain ``scan``, which runs nothing.

Returns
-------
polars.LazyFrame
    A new lazy frame over a copy the caller owns (R2), handed over as
    ``to_polars``'s.

Raises
------
PlanError
    ``KY-E215``: a ``memory_limit``, ``threads`` or ``progress`` that is not
    accepted.
MemoryLimitError
    ``KY-E401``: the plan cannot run within ``memory_limit``.
NotImplementedYetError
    ``KY-E601``: the plan has a step the executor does not run yet.

Examples
--------
>>> scan(store).cells.lazy().select("cell_id").collect()["cell_id"].to_list()
['AAAC-1', 'AAAG-1']

### CellExpr

```python
class CellExpr(Generic[_D_co])
```

An expression with one value per cell.

Built with ``cell_column``, ``gene_expression``, ``cell_embedding`` or ``feature``
and combined with operators; it records what to compute and reads nothing. The type
parameter is the dtype kind (``kyto.dtypes``): ``.str`` exists only on ``String``
(and ``Unknown``) expressions, ``&``, ``|`` and ``~`` only on ``Boolean`` ones,
arithmetic only on ``Numeric`` ones. Combining it with a ``GeneExpr`` raises
``AxisError`` (``KY-E202``, R5).

Examples
--------
>>> cell_column("n_genes") > 200
cell_column('n_genes') > 200

### CellExpr.dtype

```python
CellExpr.dtype: type[_D_co]
```

The dtype kind: a class from ``kyto.dtypes``.

Examples
--------
 >>> cell_column("total_counts").dtype
 <class 'kyto.dtypes.Unknown'>
 >>> (cell_column("total_counts") > 0).dtype
 <class 'kyto.dtypes.Boolean'>

### CellExpr.is_null

```python
CellExpr.is_null() -> CellExpr[Boolean]
```

Whether each value is missing (null): a boolean expression.

Missing metadata is null (R9): a categorical code ``-1``, a masked
nullable entry or a float ``NaN`` of an imported ``.h5ad``. A ``NaN``
that kyto itself writes stays a value, not null. Matrix values and embeddings are never null (an absent
sparse value is 0), so on them the result is always ``False``. Comparing
with ``None`` (``x == None``) raises ``KY-E212``; use this instead.

Returns
-------
The same expression class, of dtype ``Boolean``, never null itself.
Nothing is read.

Raises
------
ExpressionError
    ``KY-E207``: the expression would be too deep.

Examples
--------
 >>> cell_column("label").is_null()
 cell_column('label').is_null()

### CellExpr.is_not_null

```python
CellExpr.is_not_null() -> CellExpr[Boolean]
```

Whether each value is present (not null): a boolean expression.

The negation of ``is_null()``; see there for what is null (R9).

Returns
-------
The same expression class, of dtype ``Boolean``, never null itself.
Nothing is read.

Raises
------
ExpressionError
    ``KY-E207``: the expression would be too deep.

Examples
--------
 >>> cell_column("label").is_not_null()
 cell_column('label').is_not_null()

### CellExpr.log1p

```python
CellExpr.log1p() -> CellExpr[Numeric]
```

The natural logarithm of one plus each value: a float expression.

``numpy.log1p``: ``-1`` gives ``-inf``, a value below ``-1`` gives
``NaN``, a missing value stays missing. scanpy's ``log1p_`` QC columns
are ``qc.total_counts().log1p()`` and the like. A ``Float32`` input
gives ``Float32``, every other number ``Float64``.

Returns
-------
The same expression class, numeric. Nothing is read.

Raises
------
ExpressionError
    ``KY-E205``: the expression is not numeric. ``KY-E207``: the
    expression would be too deep.

Examples
--------
 >>> cell_column("total_counts").log1p()
 cell_column('total_counts').log1p()

### CellExpr.recompute

```python
CellExpr.recompute() -> CellExpr[_D_co]
```

This column, computed again from its lineage instead of read as stored.

A derived column the store computed (one whose ``schema.json`` entry
records ``lineage``, such as ``n_genes``) goes stale once a step such as
a gene ``filter`` changes its inputs: reading it then raises ``KY-E301``.
A recomputed read is valid there. Nothing is computed now: the executor
(task 5.x) computes it when the plan runs.

Returns
-------
The same expression class and dtype. Nothing is read.

Raises
------
ExpressionError
    ``KY-E213``: the expression is not a plain column read.

Examples
--------
>>> cell_column("n_genes").recompute()
cell_column('n_genes').recompute()

String functions; only on ``String`` (or ``Unknown``) expressions.

``numpy.log1p``: ``-1`` gives ``-inf``, a value below ``-1`` gives
``NaN``, a missing value stays missing. scanpy's ``log1p_`` QC columns
are ``qc.total_counts().log1p()`` and the like. A ``Float32`` input
gives ``Float32``, every other number ``Float64``.

Returns
-------
The same expression class, numeric. Nothing is read.

Raises
------
ExpressionError
    ``KY-E205``: the expression is not numeric. ``KY-E207``: the
    expression would be too deep.

Examples
--------
 >>> gene_column("total_counts").log1p()
 gene_column('total_counts').log1p()

### GeneExpr.recompute

```python
GeneExpr.recompute() -> GeneExpr[_D_co]
```

This column, computed again from its lineage instead of read as stored.

A derived column the store computed (one whose ``schema.json`` entry
records ``lineage``, such as ``n_genes``) goes stale once a step such as
a gene ``filter`` changes its inputs: reading it then raises ``KY-E301``.
A recomputed read is valid there. Nothing is computed now: the executor
(task 5.x) computes it when the plan runs.

Returns
-------
The same expression class and dtype. Nothing is read.

Raises
------
ExpressionError
    ``KY-E213``: the expression is not a plain column read.

Examples
--------
>>> cell_column("n_genes").recompute()
cell_column('n_genes').recompute()

### GeneExpr.str

```python
GeneExpr.str: GeneStringNamespace
```

String functions; only on ``String`` (or ``Unknown``) expressions.

Examples
--------
 >>> gene_column("label").str.starts_with("MT-")
 gene_column('label').str.starts_with('MT-')

class GeneStringNamespace

gene_column('symbol').str.starts_with('MT-')

## QC metrics (`kyto.qc`)

### qc.cells_detected

```python
qc.cells_detected(*, layer: str | None = None) -> GeneExpr[Numeric]
```

Each gene's number of cells with a non-zero value, as a ``GeneExpr``.

scanpy's ``n_cells_by_counts`` (``scanpy.pp.calculate_qc_metrics``), computed when
a plan reads it, over the cells present then (one pass over them), so it never goes
stale. ``atlas.filter(cells_detected() >= 3)`` is scanpy's
``filter_genes(min_cells=3)``.

Parameters
----------
layer : str or None, default=None
    The layer to count in. ``None`` reads the plan's default layer
    (``Atlas.with_default_layer``).

Returns
-------
GeneExpr
    A numeric (``UInt32``) expression that reads nothing until a plan using it runs.

Examples
--------
>>> cells_detected(layer="counts") >= 3
cells_detected(layer='counts') >= 3

### qc.gene_mean_counts

```python
qc.gene_mean_counts(*, layer: str | None = None) -> GeneExpr[Numeric]
```

Each gene's mean value over every cell, as a ``GeneExpr``.

scanpy's ``mean_counts`` (``scanpy.pp.calculate_qc_metrics``):
``gene_total_counts() / <number of cells>``, zeros included, ``NaN`` without
cells. Computed when a plan reads it, over the cells present then (one pass over
them), so it never goes stale; in ``float64`` (scanpy: ``float32``). scanpy's
``log1p_mean_counts`` is ``gene_mean_counts().log1p()``.

Parameters
----------
layer : str or None, default=None
    The layer to average. ``None`` reads the plan's default layer
    (``Atlas.with_default_layer``).

Returns
-------
GeneExpr
    A numeric expression that reads nothing until a plan using it runs.

Examples
--------
>>> gene_mean_counts(layer="counts") > 0.1
gene_mean_counts(layer='counts') > 0.1

### qc.gene_total_counts

```python
qc.gene_total_counts(*, layer: str | None = None) -> GeneExpr[Numeric]
```

Each gene's total count: the sum of its values over every cell, as a ``GeneExpr``.

scanpy's per-gene ``total_counts`` (``scanpy.pp.calculate_qc_metrics``), computed
when a plan reads it, over the cells present then (one pass over them), so it never
goes stale. Summed in ``float64`` (scanpy: ``float32``). scanpy's
``log1p_total_counts`` is ``gene_total_counts().log1p()``.

Parameters
----------
layer : str or None, default=None
    The layer to sum. ``None`` reads the plan's default layer
    (``Atlas.with_default_layer``).

Returns
-------
GeneExpr
    A numeric expression that reads nothing until a plan using it runs.

Examples
--------
>>> gene_total_counts(layer="counts").log1p()
gene_total_counts(layer='counts').log1p()

### qc.percent_counts_in

```python
qc.percent_counts_in(genes: _GeneExprBoolean, /, *, layer: str | None = None) -> CellExpr[Numeric]
```

Each cell's percentage of counts in a gene set, as a ``CellExpr``.

scanpy's ``pct_counts_<qc_var>`` (``scanpy.pp.calculate_qc_metrics``):
``total_counts_in(genes) / total_counts() * 100``, ``NaN`` for a cell without
counts. Computed when a plan reads it, over the genes present then, so it never
goes stale; in ``float64`` (scanpy: ``float32``).

Parameters
----------
genes : GeneExpr
    The gene set: a boolean expression on gene-table columns, such as
    ``gene_column('symbol').str.starts_with('MT-')``. A gene where it is null is
    not in the set. Checked when the plan is built.
layer : str or None, default=None
    The layer to sum. ``None`` reads the plan's default layer
    (``Atlas.with_default_layer``).

Returns
-------
CellExpr
    A numeric expression that reads nothing until a plan using it runs.

Raises
------
ExpressionError
    ``KY-E205`` if ``genes`` is not a ``GeneExpr`` or not boolean (a column of
    unknown dtype is checked when the plan is built, as is an expression that
    reads matrix values).

Examples
--------
>>> mitochondrial = gene_column("symbol").str.starts_with("MT-")
>>> percent_counts_in(mitochondrial, layer="counts") < 5
percent_counts_in(gene_column('symbol').str.starts_with('MT-'), layer='counts') < 5

### qc.percent_dropout

```python
qc.percent_dropout(*, layer: str | None = None) -> GeneExpr[Numeric]
```

Each gene's percentage of cells without a value, as a ``GeneExpr``.

scanpy's ``pct_dropout_by_counts`` (``scanpy.pp.calculate_qc_metrics``):
``(1 - cells_detected() / <number of cells>) * 100``, ``NaN`` without cells.
Computed when a plan reads it, over the cells present then (one pass over them),
so it never goes stale.

Parameters
----------
layer : str or None, default=None
    The layer to count in. ``None`` reads the plan's default layer
    (``Atlas.with_default_layer``).

Returns
-------
GeneExpr
    A numeric expression that reads nothing until a plan using it runs.

Examples
--------
>>> percent_dropout(layer="counts") < 99
percent_dropout(layer='counts') < 99

## Errors (`kyto.errors`, also at top level)

### AxisError

```python
class AxisError(KytoError, TypeError)
```

An expression mixes the cells and genes axes (R5).

Subclasses `KytoError` and `TypeError`. Raised with these codes:

- ``KY-E202``: A cell expression and a gene expression are combined.

See `KytoError` for the parameters and attributes.

Examples
--------
>>> error = AxisError("KY-E202", operation="&", cell_expression="cell_column('n_genes') > 200", gene_expression="gene_column('highly_variable')")
>>> error.code
'KY-E202'
>>> isinstance(error, TypeError)
True

### CorruptStoreError

```python
class CorruptStoreError(KytoError, ValueError)
```

A store on disk breaks the store format (docs/format.md).

Subclasses `KytoError` and `ValueError`. Raised with these codes:

- ``KY-E107``: A stored layer breaks the tiled sparse format (format.md section 4).
- ``KY-E113``: A stored cell or gene table breaks format.md section 5.
- ``KY-E116``: A path is not a kyto store: its root zarr.json is missing or has no format_version (format.md section 3).
- ``KY-E122``: A store's schema.json is missing, is not JSON, or breaks format.md section 8.
- ``KY-E126``: A stored embedding or graph breaks the store format (format.md sections 6 and 7), or disagrees with schema.json.
- ``KY-E127``: A store was changed on disk after a plan scanned it.

See `KytoError` for the parameters and attributes.

Examples
--------
>>> error = CorruptStoreError("KY-E107", layer="counts", problem="tile (0, 2): indptr ends at 5 but tile_offsets gives 7 entries")
>>> error.code
'KY-E107'
>>> isinstance(error, ValueError)
True

### DeviceError

```python
class DeviceError(KytoError, RuntimeError)
```

The requested device cannot run part of the plan.

Subclasses `KytoError` and `RuntimeError`. Raised with these codes:

- ``KY-E501``: The requested device has no kernel for an operation.
- ``KY-E502``: The CPU executor cannot start the threads it was asked for.

See `KytoError` for the parameters and attributes.

Examples
--------
>>> error = DeviceError("KY-E501", operation="leiden", device="cuda")
>>> error.code
'KY-E501'
>>> isinstance(error, RuntimeError)
True

### DuplicateIdError

```python
class DuplicateIdError(KytoError, ValueError)
```

Cell or gene IDs that must be unique are not.

Subclasses `KytoError` and `ValueError`. Raised with these codes:

- ``KY-E101``: IDs written to a store are not unique.

See `KytoError` for the parameters and attributes.

Examples
--------
>>> error = DuplicateIdError("KY-E101", axis="genes", n_duplicated=12, ids=["ENSG01", "ENSG02"])
>>> error.code
'KY-E101'
>>> isinstance(error, ValueError)
True

### ExpressionError

```python
class ExpressionError(KytoError, TypeError)
```

An expression is given an operand, or used in a context, that it does not support.

Subclasses `KytoError` and `TypeError`. Raised with these codes:

- ``KY-E205``: An expression operation is given an operand of a dtype or type it does not accept.
- ``KY-E206``: An expression is used where Python needs True or False.
- ``KY-E207``: An expression tree is deeper than kyto builds.
- ``KY-E209``: An embedding component is not a non-negative int.
- ``KY-E212``: An expression is compared with None, which is not a test for missing values.
- ``KY-E213``: `.recompute()` is called on an expression that is not a plain column read.

See `KytoError` for the parameters and attributes.

Examples
--------
>>> error = ExpressionError("KY-E205", operation="str.starts_with", accepted="a string expression", got="a numeric expression", operand="cell_column('n_genes') + 1")
>>> error.code
'KY-E205'
>>> isinstance(error, TypeError)
True

### FormatVersionError

```python
class FormatVersionError(KytoError, ValueError)
```

A store has a format_version this kyto does not read (format.md section 11).

Subclasses `KytoError` and `ValueError`. Raised with these codes:

- ``KY-E115``: A store has a format_version this kyto does not read (format.md section 11).

See `KytoError` for the parameters and attributes.

Examples
--------
>>> error = FormatVersionError("KY-E115", store="pbmc.kyto", found="0.2", supported=["0.1"])
>>> error.code
'KY-E115'
>>> isinstance(error, ValueError)
True

### InputFileError

```python
class InputFileError(KytoError, ValueError)
```

An input file given to convert has a format, encoding or value kyto cannot import.

Subclasses `KytoError` and `ValueError`. Raised with these codes:

- ``KY-E120``: An input file given to convert has a format or an encoding kyto does not import.
- ``KY-E121``: An input file given to convert holds a value or a structure that breaks its own format or cannot be stored.

See `KytoError` for the parameters and attributes.

Examples
--------
>>> error = InputFileError("KY-E120", path="pbmc.h5ad:/X", problem="encoding-type 'awkward-array' is not supported", accepted="store X as an array, csr_matrix or csc_matrix (anndata >= 0.8 writes these)")
>>> error.code
'KY-E120'
>>> isinstance(error, ValueError)
True

### KytoError

```python
class KytoError(Exception)
```

Base class of every kyto error.

Catch it to handle any kyto error. Only its subclasses are raised, each with a
registered ``KY-Exxx`` code.

Parameters
----------
code : str
    A registered ``KY-Exxx`` code of this class.
**fields : str | int | Sequence[str]
    The structured fields of that code, by name.

Attributes
----------
code : str
    The stable ``KY-Exxx`` code.
message : str
    What was wrong and where, without the code.
hint : str
    How to fix it.
docs_url : str
    The link to this code's documentation.
fields : Mapping[str, FieldValue]
    The structured fields, read-only (`list[str]` values as tuples).

Raises
------
TypeError
    If the code is not registered for this class, or a field is missing,
    unknown or of the wrong type (a bug in kyto, not in the caller's input).

Examples
--------
>>> try:
...     raise ResolutionError("KY-E201", name="CD3E", candidates=["log1p:CD3E"])
... except KytoError as error:
...     print(error.code, error.fields["name"])
KY-E201 CD3E

A layer is read with a value dtype other than the one it stores.

Subclasses `KytoError` and `TypeError`. Raised with these codes:

True

>>> isinstance(error, ValueError)

### PlanError

```python
class PlanError(KytoError, ValueError)
```

A plan method is given an argument outside what it accepts, or cannot extend this plan.

Subclasses `KytoError` and `ValueError`. Raised with these codes:

- ``KY-E215``: A plan method is given an argument value outside what it accepts.
- ``KY-E216``: A plan that ends in a sink is extended with another step.
- ``KY-E217``: Text given to from_json is not a plan JSON, or breaks its format.
- ``KY-E218``: A plan JSON has a version this kyto does not read.
- ``KY-E219``: peek() is called on a plan whose cell table cannot be read from metadata alone.

See `KytoError` for the parameters and attributes.

Examples

### StoreInputError

```python
class StoreInputError(KytoError, ValueError)
```

Data, names, parameters or selections given to a store writer or reader break the store format (docs/format.md).

Subclasses `KytoError` and `ValueError`. Raised with these codes:

- ``KY-E102``: A layer, embedding or graph name breaks the naming rules of format.md section 2.1.
- ``KY-E103``: A member with the same name, compared case-insensitively, is already in the store.
- ``KY-E104``: A store writer parameter (tile or chunk size, compression level) is out of range.
- ``KY-E105``: A size is above a limit of the store format (format.md section 4.5).
- ``KY-E106``: A sparse matrix given to a store writer is not valid CSR of the stated shape.
- ``KY-E111``: The ID column of a cell or gene table holds null or empty IDs.
- ``KY-E112``: A column of a cell or gene table breaks format.md section 5 (name, dtype or position).
- ``KY-E114``: A cell or gene selection given to the tile reader is out of range, unsorted or repeats a position.
- ``KY-E117``: A CellBlock is not valid CSR, or does not fit the store or layer it is written to (format.md sections 4.8 and 10.2).
- ``KY-E118``: A store writer's target path already exists (format.md section 10.1).
- ``KY-E119``: A cell or gene table given to a store writer does not have one row per matrix row or column (format.md section 5.1).
- ``KY-E123``: An export's target path already exists (sink_h5ad, task 2.7).
- ``KY-E124``: A store holds a name or value the export format cannot hold (sink_h5ad, task 2.7).
- ``KY-E125``: A remote store URL or one of its storage options cannot be used to open an object store (task 2.8).

See `KytoError` for the parameters and attributes.

Examples
--------
>>> error = StoreInputError("KY-E102", kind="layer", name="log1p/counts", rule="character '/' is not allowed")
>>> error.code
'KY-E102'
>>> isinstance(error, ValueError)
True
